svg.text: Poincaré sections do NOT discriminate at 300 crossings: chaotic TS and regular Kerr look alike
One orbit per panel, 300 crossings, tol 1e-13. TS (blue): confirmed chaotic by fd + S_ex + complex drift. Kerr (orange): regular controls with the largest S_ex.
The chaotic layers are thin, so a 300-crossing section traces a near-curve. This is why sections alone
(as in Dubeibe et al. 2007) read regular. The discriminating views: fig150_fate.svg, fig150_alpha.svg.
